Public First Action said that it endorses officials who support regulating AI and that “the aligned PACs run ads on the issues that matter most immediately to voters in each race”. Leading the Future did not respond to requests for comment.

Michael Beckel, Director of Money in Politics Reform at Issue One told us that this leaves voters at a disadvantage. “Special interests seem keen on moving voters with messaging around hot-button issues, all while advancing a specific policy agenda that viewers of ads are kept in the dark about.”

Many of the ads analysed mentioned issues like cutting taxes and promoting local businesses. When referencing immigration and Trump, ads were highly divisive. Both networks put out ads through their subsidiary super PACs that seem to directly contradict each other.
Bellingcat analysed 336 video ads from the two leading AI-backed Super PACs. Of all election ads analysed, only two out of the 40 candidates had videos that mentioned AI.

A Bellingcat analysis of video ads purchased by the two largest AI-backed Super PACS has revealed that their political advertisements rarely ever mention their stances on AI, despite the advertisements being paid for by issue-specific PACs. www.bellingcat.com/news/2026/11...
